indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so its letters come backwards

parts.note: pay as a noun can mean a reward or recompense

explanation.surface: A creative person is pleased to be getting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns REWARD upwards in this down entry, giving DRAWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sketches or makes designs on paper is a draughtsman, one who draws.

parts.note: being late here means being dead, not tardy, and the praise is carved on a gravestone

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for turning up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means deceased: the commendation is the words of praise inscribed on a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tomb usually praises the dead person, a tribute to the deceased.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
on can mean over or upon
fast in the sense of firmly fixed means stable

explanation.surface: An artist dashes off many pictures far too quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' suggests speed but means firmly fixed. John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was a celebrated English landscape artist of the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: A little page content in dry Mexican cape

indicators.note: being the content of something means being held inside it

parts.note: sere is a poetic word meaning dry or withered
P is the standard short form of page

explanation.surface: A brief page of writing sits inside a dry cloak from Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content in' puts A and P inside SERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A serape is a brightly coloured woollen shawl or blanket worn as a cloak in Mexico.

clue.text: Pawn money aright and it will grow

parts.note: to pop something is slang for pawning it
L stands for pound, the British unit of money
split as a plus right, giving A and R, the usual short form of right

explanation.surface: Hock your possessions properly and your wealth will increase.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about money growing, but what grows is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing tree, and trees grow.

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
to lance is to cut open, as a surgeon does a boil

explanation.surface: A conversation about the usual way to cut something.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a way of speaking or a particular idiom, the manner of someone's speech.

parts.note: dope and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone drugs a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The potto is a slow-moving primate of the African forests.

clue.text: Tea's been prepared, but there's someone missing

indicators.note: tea that is prepared is made up, so these letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: The tea is made but one guest has not turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges TEASBEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is not present where expected.

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is a salesman, short form rep
a rover is one who wanders far and wide

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 19 across, a salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to scold or rebuke, so one who rebukes fits.

indicators.note: organising means putting things in order, so the letters here are set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Pottery workers stage a tidy show of unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-organised' rearranges POTTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is a public objection or demonstration against something.

indicators.note: the word that accepts something takes it inside itself

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, one who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A man who never drank once held office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepting' is the container signal; 'in' is only a link, since the watt is the unit in which power is measured.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical power is measured in units named after James Watt, the engineer.

clue.text: Blow backing a horse! This is most important

indicators.note: backing means the word goes in reverse here

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock or blow
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Betting on a horse is a terrible blow, which matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' suggests betting but reverses RAP to PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of chief importance.

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a degree held by a churchman

explanation.surface: A churchman's twenty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is TOT, read here as a verb meaning to sum up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up a column of figures is to sum it.

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is a salesman, short form rep
laced means tied or bound up

explanation.surface: A salesman tied up and then put back in his job.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 19 across, a salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reinstated is to be restored to one's former position.

clue.text: Bank giving many a cautious signal

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
the amber traffic light warns drivers to proceed with caution

explanation.surface: A bank offering customers a warning signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; it means a slope. Amber is the yellow traffic light between green and red in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the slight slope of a road surface, a banking.

indicators.note: something broke is smashed, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A penniless man's patter gives away where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like penniless but rearranges MANPATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a set of rooms on one floor, a dwelling.

indicators.note: in signals the award sits inside the word for force

parts.note: to coerce is to force someone
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: A firm receives a prize for its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'award' here is the British Military Medal, not a prize in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling of goods.

clue.text: A great deal may be offered for sale

explanation.surface: Something is sold at a large discount.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty, a large quantity; also an item put up at an auction.

explanation.surface: An army officer's old-fashioned bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The early high-wheeled bicycle was called an ordinary; 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual or common; also the old name for the high-wheeled Victorian bicycle.

clue.text: The salesman concerned with small change

parts.note: re means about or concerning
P is a penny, the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A salesman worries about a bit of loose change.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales representative is commonly abbreviated to a shortened form.

explanation.surface: Something that has ended and something that came before.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex-, no longer in that role; also earlier, preceding.

explanation.surface: A drink for a dozen people.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 down is ADD; this light, as a verb, means to sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits; also to sum up, as in reckoning figures.

clue.text: Odd characters con a dim vagrant

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are turned into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Strange people swindle a dull-witted tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' rearranges CONADIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic describes those who wander without a fixed home.

clue.text: Slip up on taking superior view

explanation.surface: Making a mistake while enjoying a high vantage point.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to notice; also to look down upon from above.

clue.text: Found buyers, so closed after five

indicators.note: after signals the second word follows the first in the answer

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ended means finished or closed

explanation.surface: The shop sold out, so it shut after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after five' looks like a time of day but sets ENDED after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that were sold were offered and taken up by purchasers.

explanation.surface: Crosses written at the end of a letter show love.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosses at the bottom of a letter stand for smacks; also loving touches of the lips.

clue.text: One made time to change on the spot

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: change signals the letters of these words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone found the time to switch places there and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges MADETIME to MMEDIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Done on the spot means done at once, without delay.

clue.text: Held by college lecturers due to take up appointments

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of these two words

explanation.surface: University teachers are about to start new posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held by' points to the letters inside collEGE LECturers.
explanation.definitionFit: The president-elect is chosen but not yet installed, due to start the job.

clue.text: Complaints for which a doctor has the answer

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
ANS is a short form of answer

explanation.surface: Grievances that a physician can resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Moans are grumbles or complaints.

clue.text: Learns a new way to produce a magazine

indicators.note: letters arranged a new way are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone learns a new technique for producing a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new way' rearranges LEARNSA. 'magazine' means a store of weapons, not a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in the military sense is a store for arms and ammunition.

clue.text: The average hour allowed as an interval

parts.note: the mean is the average value
an hour, as in the hour has come, is a time

explanation.surface: The typical hour allowed for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The meantime is the period between two events.

parts.note: sent means despatched

explanation.surface: A timepiece posted by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' suggests a timepiece but means a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier keeping guard, on watch.
